precepts.why:
“The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted.” He has chosen and set apart every man here, all the captains, to preach good tidings to the meek. But how do you bind up a person that is broken? The brokenhearted are broken in the mind: suffering the curses without knowing the will of God. We are set apart to bind them up. What do we bind them with?

“Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” We bind up the testimony and seal the law in the minds of the people, because they are brokenhearted and their minds are broken. That is what we are called to do: to bind them to the laws of God.

And we show them why it is good. Look at our lives as the example of what it means to serve God and why it is good to serve him. That means we have to be sincere about it. How do we tell the people to touch not the unclean thing and then not live it ourselves? The one who was profitable to many but not to himself will be punished accordingly, because he knew better.

So the good tidings we proclaim with the law are these: if we repent and keep God's laws in sincerity and endure to the end, he will deliver us, and we will rule again, as we were made in his image to rule.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Isaiah 61 says to “proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord”, and Isaiah 49 says it again: “Thus saith the Lord, In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee: and I will preserve thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, to establish the earth, to cause to inherit the desolate heritages.” The acceptable year and the acceptable time: that is when we heal the broken heart and proclaim liberty to the captives.

“The Lord hath called me from the womb; from the bowels of my mother hath he made mention of my name. And he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand hath he hid me, and made me a polished shaft; in his quiver hath he hid me; And said unto me, Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified.” We are supposed to glorify our God in this body.

“Then I said, I have laboured in vain, I have spent my strength for nought, and in vain: yet surely my judgment is with the Lord, and my work with my God.” We go to stiff-necked, hard-hearted people who refuse to hear the word of God, but we still proclaim the day of the Lord to heal those minds and tell them there is an end to this: we will rule one day. He formed us from the womb “to bring Jacob again to him.”

“It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel.” It may not appear that we are doing it, but when the numbers come in, it is a light thing he has given us, and he still charges us to raise up the children of Israel. “I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth”: that goes back to Matthew 4, the Gentiles of Galilee. Our job is to bring salvation to the people and lead them back to him, and that is a great ministry.

“Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship” … “and he shall choose thee.” Out of all of them, he is going to choose us. And unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: we want to be the faithful servant the Lord finds doing this work in sincerity, without deceit and without secret sins.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
2 Esdras 3:6 says God led Adam “into paradise, which thy right hand had planted”, and Genesis 2:8 says the same thing: “the Lord God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.” Adam's kingdom ruled the heaven and the earth. The man who could go to paradise, where the Lord is, did not walk around without clothes. Then verse 9: “And out of the ground made the Lord God to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight and good for food”. What is that talking about?

Isaiah 61:3: “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the Lord”. The trees of righteousness are Israel: us, in paradise, in our heavenly bodies.

Reading Genesis 2:9 again: the trees pleasant to the sight and good for food are a similitude for Adam's sons in the heavens, the righteous. “the tree of life also in the midst of the garden”: the twelve apostles were up there, the 144 were there, all twelve tribes were there. “and the tree of knowledge of good and evil”: that is Satan. The tree people set up and worship in their houses at Christmas references that tree; Babylon referenced it, and Santa Claus is Satan Claus.

God works hand in hand with the prophets. He has Moses write something hard, and he has the other prophets come and explain what it is talking about. Isaiah explains the trees of Genesis: the planting of the Lord is his people.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Isaiah 61 is fulfilled in Christ, who read it himself: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor.” The good tidings of Isaiah are the gospel. And the poor are not everybody: “the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.” The poor are the poor of Zion. You do not even have to go to Isaiah 14; Isaiah 61 itself says it is them that mourn in Zion.

“he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives.” We are the captives. How can you read captive and think everybody? Rome was dominating Israel at that time. “and recovering of sight to the blind”: we are the blind people. “to set at liberty them that are bruised”: bruised in sin.

“To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.” The acceptable year of the Lord is our day of jubilee, and we had better accept that.

Imagine the Israelites and the Romans sitting in church together, the captives and the captors side by side, told we are all the same. It makes no sense. Jake looks over at Esau to see if he is upset, and if master is upset at this reading, he disregards it: black Christians hate anything that upsets white folks, and that is why they do not believe. But Christ read it plainly: he came to proclaim liberty to the captives of Israel, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound, bound in these prisons we call America, the Caribbean and whatever lands we are in.

“the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek.” Christ read it in Luke 4 as “to preach the gospel to the poor.” When it says the poor, who is that? Isaiah answers: “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

That is telling you who the poor are: the poor of Zion, the poor of his people. Zion is another name for the Israelites.

And Isaiah 61 itself agrees: he came “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes”. Why are we mourning? Because we are captive.

So the good tidings, the brokenhearted, the captives and them that are bound are not all nations. They are the poor of the Lord’s people, the Israelites in captivity, who shall trust in the Zion the Lord has founded.

Today you want to talk to your boss and he turns his back to you; on that day they are going to beg for your attention.

Zephaniah is the precept to that: “Behold, at that time I will undo all that afflict thee.” He is going to undo all the nations that afflict us. “and I will save her that halteth”: we are the ones that halt, because we are captive. “and gather her that was driven out.”

“and I will get them praise and fame in every land where they have been put to shame.” We get that fame and that glory, and our children are going to get it too. Everybody is going to acknowledge who we are. “At that time will I bring you again, even in the time that I gather you: for I will make you a name and a praise among all people of the earth, when I turn back your captivity before your eyes, saith the Lord.”

That is the liberty proclaimed to the captives in Isaiah 61: not only freed, but honoured in the very lands that shamed us.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Isaiah 61 proclaims “the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God.” There is a particular day in a particular year when God will come to deliver his people. Isaiah 63 shows that day: “Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? this that is glorious in his apparel, travelling in the greatness of his strength?” This is Christ, the Son of God, and his garment is glorious, not a sheet or a robe.

“Wherefore art thou red in thine apparel, and thy garments like him that treadeth in the winefat?” Isaiah is asking Christ, Why are you red? It looks like you were stomping grapes. “I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me.” Christ trod down the nations and killed them alone. He did not need the help of the twelve tribes of Israel; he did it himself.

“for I will tread them in mine anger, and trample them in my fury; and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments.” The wine represents their blood.

“For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.” We are the redeemed. The year of my redeemed is the acceptable year of the Lord in Isaiah 61, our jubilee, and it comes with the day of vengeance on the nations.

“Their slain also shall be cast out, and their stink shall come up out of their carcases, and the mountains shall be melted with their blood.” You know anything that can melt somebody? Thermonuclear fire. Vengeance, baby, vengeance. “And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved”: all your satellites, America’s Space Force, shall be dissolved. “And the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll”: that’s that mushroom cloud. Boom, baby, boom. That’s what it’s talking about. “And all their host shall fall down”: their satellites, their rockets, everything America got up there in space shall fall down, “as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree.” This is the day of vengeance. This is therapy for the sick, the brokenhearted; therapy for our soul, for our minds. The sound of salvation. The gospel.

“For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea”. Idumea is a Greek name for Edom. The urban apologetics and the Jehovah Witnesses say they were done away during the time of Saul; so is God crazy here? It shall, future tense, come down upon Idumea. So Idumea is in power today. Edom is in power. Who is Edom? America, that’s Edom; that’s the white Caucasians, Russia, Britain, London, all these coconuts, Germany, they’re Edom. “And upon the people of my curse, to judgment”: he’s going to judge them.

“The sword of the Lord is filled with blood, it is made fat with fatness, and with the blood of lambs and goats”: the blood of lambs and goats is the nations, a metaphor for them. “For the Lord hath a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Idumea”: the land of the white man, America, Britain, all these places. “And the unicorns shall come down with them,” “and the bullocks with the bulls; and their land shall be soaked with blood”: America, France, Germany gonna be soaked with blood.

Then verse 8 again: “For it is the day of the Lord’s vengeance”. This is what comforts all that mourn. “And the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion”: the year of recompence means judgment, payback, the big payback. Who does the land of Zion belong to? It’s a controversy, a world controversy.

Your God will come with vengeance, “even God with a recompence; he will come and save you.” God’s gonna come and save us.

That’s what the Bible says. Somebody will say, when the thermonuclear destruction comes, World War Three and the second coming, y’all gonna get it too. Oh no, we not. The Bible says God will come and save us.

note.label: | Good News for Our Oppressed People | Part Three

precepts.why:
Watch what Christ said. There ain’t no Christian on earth talking about this thing. Christ gives us a story, and you want to wonder what we should pray for? Well, here you go: pray for vengeance. “And he spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint; Saying, There was in a city a judge, which feared not God, neither regarded man: And there was a widow in that city; and she came unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary.” That’s the key word we want: avenge me of mine adversary. Give me vengeance against my enemies. That’s hate speech.

“And he would not for a while”: this unjust judge would not, for a while. “But afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man”: I don’t regard any man on earth. “Yet because this widow troubleth me”: because this widow annoys me day after day, crying and pleading with me to give her vengeance, “I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me”; she’s tiring me out.

Then the Lord breaks down what the whole parable means: “And shall not God avenge his own elect”. Who is God’s elect? Israel, mine elect. Shall not God avenge Israel, “which cry day and night unto him”, which pray day and night, “though he bear long with them? I tell you that he will avenge them speedily.” God will avenge the Israelites speedily. “Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?”

Raise your hand: how many of you pray for vengeance against the enemies? All of us should be praying for vengeance; that’s what the Bible says. You don’t think, when we saw what happened to Breonna Taylor, we wanted to do something? You don’t think we sat there mad, on the brink of tears, wanting to get together and do something? But the Bible says pray for vengeance. Pray for vengeance.

note.label: | Good News for Our Oppressed People | Part Three

note.label: | Good News for Our Oppressed People | Part Three

precepts.why:
“He will swallow up death in victory; and the Lord God will wipe away tears from off all faces”. See what the Lord is going to do: he’s going to wipe away the tears that we feel. This is talking about us.

Sometimes I sit alone and I watch the news, I look at the atrocities to our people, and it does bring tears to your eyes; not tears so much of grief, but of anger. Anger coupled with grief. When y’all watched George Floyd die, it was murder, and you hear that man cry for his mother, and his mother was already dead. Just imagine what was going through his mind as he was slowly dying. That thing almost brought tears to my eyes, because I’m so angry. That’s what we’re waiting for.

“And the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth”. What is our rebuke? Slavery, captivity, oppression. He said, I’m going to take it away from off the earth. “For the Lord hath spoken it.”

note.label: | Good News for Our Oppressed People | Part Three

precepts.why: “And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying”. There shall be no more George Floyd deaths, no more Breonna Taylor deaths, no more Tamir Rice deaths, no more Sandra Bland deaths. “Neither shall there be any more pain”: no more pain with someone’s foot, someone’s knee on the back of our necks, or someone choking us and we screaming, I can’t breathe. “For the former things are passed away”: the Bible says them days are going to be finished, done with, gone.

note.label: | Good News for Our Oppressed People | Part Three

precepts.why:
Why we should be called the trees of righteousness. “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners”, breaking God’s laws, “nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful. But his delight is in the law of the Lord; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.”

Watch this: “And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water”. If we walk in and delight in the law of God, we shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water. When you examine the trees planted by the rivers of water, those are strong trees; they bring forth the greatest and biggest fruit. “That bringeth forth his fruit in his season”: the fruit is not delayed or halted.

It’s talking about the understanding. “His leaf also shall not wither”: the leaves on those trees shall not wither, nor shall our understanding. “And whatsoever he doeth shall prosper”: whatsoever we do in this day shall prosper.

note.label: | Good News for Our Oppressed People | Part Three

precepts.why:
The chapter before gives the understanding of the alien being our plowmen. “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls”: this is the gospel. “And their kings shall minister unto thee.” Then: “for in my wrath I smote thee”. In God’s wrath he smote us and sent us into slavery; that is what that means. “But in my favour have I had mercy on thee”: that is when he sent Christ.

“Therefore thy gates shall be open continually”: the gates of all kingdoms shall be opened continually. “They shall not be shut day nor night.” Why? “That men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles”: men are going to bring us the wealth, the riches of the nations. “And that their kings may be brought”: their kings are going to be brought before us. “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.”

What are we reading? The gospel, the good news. This is medicine for the mind, for the soul; this is therapy.

“The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together”: the nations are going to bring these elements to us, “to beautify the place of my sanctuary”, for the purpose of beautifying God’s sanctuary. “And I will make the place of my feet glorious.”

“The sons also of them that afflicted thee”: the white man, the Chinese and Japanese and Arabs, the sons of them that afflicted thee “shall come bending unto thee”. And all they that despised us, all they that hate our guts, “shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.” They are going to call all Israel the city of the Lord. That is who the strangers and the sons of the alien are: the nations that afflicted us, coming to serve.

note.label: | Good News for Our Oppressed People | Part Three

precepts.why:
Right now Hosea 4:6 applies to us. Isaiah says “ye shall be named the Priests of the Lord”, but Hosea 4:6 is where we are at today. “My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge.” What’s the knowledge? The knowledge of God is the laws of God.

“Because thou hast rejected knowledge”: because we have rejected the laws of God, “I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me”. “Seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God”: because you have forgotten the law of your God. That verse right there proves that the knowledge of God is the law of God.

And because we have forgotten the knowledge of God, the laws of God, we are no priests. What does that mean? We have become slaves: oppressed, crushed, smitten with madness and blindness of heart.

note.label: | Good News for Our Oppressed People | Part Three

precepts.why:
What does it mean that we have no priest? Because the prophecy from the time of Moses said this: “And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests”. This is the prophecy.

At that time the priest was who? The Levites. You don’t think the Levites were like, what are you talking about, a nation? We had a priest. Moses was speaking above and beyond. Why? Because he had just come down from the mountain, and the Lord showed him the kingdom of heaven, where all the Israelite males, the elect, shall be a kingdom of priests. And that is not all: “and an holy nation.”

note.label: | Good News for Our Oppressed People | Part Three

precepts.why:
That is what Moses said prophetically; watch what Christ said prophetically. “And hath made us kings and priests.” Why? Because the prophecy from the time of Moses said that we shall be a kingdom of priests.

Remember what Christ said: ‘I’m not come to destroy the law or the prophets... but to fulfil.’ Moses prophesied, you shall be a kingdom of priests, and Christ is saying, I am coming to make sure it comes to pass. That is what Isaiah 61:6 is talking about: “ye shall be named the Priests of the Lord”.

note.label: | Good News for Our Oppressed People | Part Three

precepts.why:

So the garden of Eden is coming back; we are going right back. What we read about in Genesis chapters one, two and three about the garden of Eden is coming back again on the earth, and we are going to be in the midst of it. That is when the twelve tribes of Israel are gathered together unto Christ. That is the land we shall possess.

Look at the map, and this ain’t a full map. Remember, America is going to be wiped off the face of the earth. But over here on the right side we are going to be made famous: in Europe, in Morocco, in Arabia. These countries are going to remain; the continent of Africa is still going to be here, and we are going to get praise and fame on the continent of Africa. We are going to get praise and fame in Madagascar, Reunion, Mauritius, Sri Lanka. They sent us to India and Pakistan: we are going to get praise and fame. They sent us to Iran and Iraq: we are going to get praise and fame. They sent us to Syria and Turkey: we are going to get praise and fame.

And with this praise and fame they are going to acknowledge our seed, our offspring, our sons and daughters, by name. That is how “their seed shall be known among the Gentiles”.

note.label: | Good News for Our Oppressed People | Part Three

“I decked thee also with ornaments, and I put bracelets upon thy hands”: we are going to have armbands and bracelets; that is what he is talking about. You got male bracelets, you got female bracelets. “And a chain on thy neck”: that’s right. That is in our spirit; we like them chains on our neck, gold chains. He ain’t talking about no iron. We are going to get some real gold, the thick gold, and pricing ain’t going to be an issue, because it is ours.

“And I put a jewel on thy forehead”: we are going to have real jewels on our forehead, none of that little plastic gem that gets stuck right there. The hell is this? They start sweating and the thing slides off their face. “And earrings in thine ears”: real earrings, not the kind that turn your ear black. You ever see sis wearing that, the ear turn all black and ashy? Like, what the hell is that in your ear? “And a beautiful crown upon thine head”: we are going to have crowns.

“Thus wast thou decked with gold and silver; and thy raiment was of fine linen, and silk, and broidered work; thou didst eat fine flour, and honey, and oil: and thou wast exceeding beautiful, and thou didst prosper into a kingdom.” We prospered into a kingdom, and we shall do so again.

“And thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty”: thy renown, meaning thy fame, went throughout the nations for our beauty. All the nations followed our example. That is why you see the Assyrians, the Romans, even the Babylonians with fringes, because they got it all from us. We are going to be beautiful on that day.
